_purpose: Cross-spec function divergences that are INTENTIONAL and DECLARED. Read by audit_deep.py check 3 (XSPEC-DRIFT). Created 2026-08-20 so that the line-based fence scanner could ship: the previous regex extractor truncated Framework_MockTestAnalyse.md's S8-1 Drive transport fence at the first ``` inside a docstring, so acquire_paper / plan_transport / probe_drive_channel were never audited at all, and reporting `findings: 0` over unread code is not the same as having no findings.
_policy: THE ONLY LEGITIMATE EDIT IS A DELETION. An entry pins the fingerprint of BOTH bodies; change either side and the exemption goes STALE and FAILS THE BUILD, because what was reviewed is no longer what is in the file. An entry whose divergence has disappeared also fails, so a dormant exemption cannot lie in wait for the next divergence of the same name. There is NO WRITER: `audit_deep.py --print-divergence-baseline` prints a candidate for a human to paste, so every entry arrives as a reviewable diff. A --write flag is exactly how spec_name_audit re-froze two defects it had just fixed (Framework_MockTestAnalyse v2.53.1, D5/D6); that switch is deliberately not built here.
_complements: mock_sync_audit MS-13 already requires BOTH specs to NAME a probe-paper divergence in prose. This file records the same fact structurally, so the two checks fail independently: prose that stops matching the code fails MS-13, code that changes under a declared exemption fails XSPEC-BASELINE-STALE.

_reasons.step_label_only: bodies differ only in a printed step identifier (S5-x vs S8-x)
_reasons.declared_step_divergence: the steps genuinely differ and BOTH specs name the divergence in prose
_reasons.declared_law_scope: a law applies to one step and is declared out of scope for the other, with the reason stated in the spec that does not carry it

probe_drive_channel.note: Docstrings are already stripped by fingerprint(), so the ONLY remaining difference is the printed banner: Step 4 prints 'S5-0 CHANNEL PROBE', Step 5 prints 'S8-0 CHANNEL PROBE'. Step 5's docstring states 'Identical contract to Framework_PYQCount S5-0'. Merging the two would require one step to print the other's section id, which is worse than the divergence.

acquire_paper.note: Different acquisition models, not drift. Step 4 (single-session, whole corpus in one run) keys off `paper['id'] in drive_payloads` with a `paper.get('path')` fallback, because PHASE A materialised every payload up front. Step 5 (batched across ~8 sessions) keys off `paper_ref['source'] != 'gdrive'`, because its batch loop carries a source-tagged reference rather than a pre-materialised payload map. Both docstrings state the shared invariant that matters — `resolver` performs no tool call, and every failure degrades to the upload lane via TransportFallback rather than being fatal.

plan_transport.note: Step 5's signature carries the v2.51.0 SESSION-BUDGET LAW (session_budget, batch_size, probe_consumed) and the P4d/P4f/P4g deviations; Step 4's does not. Framework_PYQCount v1.5 propagated THREE of the four laws from GAP-2026-08-16-STEP5-SESSION-EXHAUSTION (EC-P43 direct egress, EC-P40 probe-as-spender with consumed= stated explicitly as 0, EC-P41 asserted listing) and declared the fourth OUT OF SCOPE with its reason on the record: Step 4 is single-session, so its probe cost amortises to zero, and its route is under SPEC_BUDGET_BYTES. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-20: PYQCount route 239,599 B against the 250,000 B threshold, and Step 4 still fetches the probe paper again in the same run. Headroom is 10,401 B (4.2%) — if PYQCount ever crosses the threshold, the fourth law becomes live for Step 4 and this entry must be re-reviewed, not extended.
